stem: What does Gower sign specifically indicate during a motor examination?

options.text: Distal muscle weakness in the hands
Proximal weakness at the hip joints

explanation: Proximal weakness at the hip joints is indicated by Gower sign. A child with this sign uses the hands to “walk” up the thighs when rising from the floor, showing weakness of the hip and pelvic girdle muscles.

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because Gower sign reflects weakness of the proximal lower limb muscles, not distal hand weakness.
optionExplanations.B: Correct because a child rising by climbing up their own legs indicates proximal pelvic and hip girdle weakness.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because spasticity is an upper motor neurone feature and is not what Gower sign is used to identify.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because ataxia affects coordination and balance, whereas Gower sign indicates muscle weakness.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because sensory loss does not cause the characteristic manoeuvre seen with Gower sign.

source.hint: Recall how a child might use their arms to compensate for weak leg and hip muscles when rising from the floor.
